title: UserPolicyDocument
description: A user-authored policy for one TwistedPear installation. Informative until an evaluator validates against it; see specs/spec-policy/spec.md. Every vocabulary below is closed on purpose: an unrecognised subject, predicate, or combinator blocks load rather than being ignored (P-R1), because a policy the host does not fully understand must never be treated as satisfied.

version.description: Policy language version. Committed into the seal, so a host that does not know this version refuses the installation rather than opening it (P-R9).

Subject.description: The closed set of action classes a rule may gate. policy:amend and policy:seal are ordinary subjects: policy governs the setting of policy.

BasePosture.description: The decision for a subject when no rule matches. Every subject must be listed: a policy that does not say what happens by default does not load.

id.description: Stable within the document. Identifies the rule in previews, consent records, and seal commits.

capability.description: Narrows a grant:request rule to one capability id. Absent means every capability.

onUnknown.description: The terminal collapse for this rule. Mandatory, with no default: a rule that does not say what an unresolved condition means does not load (P-R2). "ask" escalates to host chrome and applies the answer to this decision only.

sealed.description: Committed into the chain deriving the installation vault key. A sealed rule cannot be removed by any amendment, and editing it on disk renders the store unreadable (P-R7, P-R8).

note.description: The author's own words, reproduced verbatim in the consequence preview.

Expression.description: Three-valued: every expression evaluates to true, false, or unknown. unknown means the evidence was not obtainable and is never silently equated with false.

NullaryPredicate.description: Predicates taking no argument. The environmental and interactive ones resolve to unknown whenever the evidence source is absent, stale, or unattested.

all.description: Strong Kleene AND: false if any operand is false, else unknown if any is unknown, else true.

any.description: Strong Kleene OR: true if any operand is true, else unknown if any is unknown, else false.

known.description: True only if the operand is true; unknown becomes false. The "must be demonstrated" combinator.

assume.description: Collapses unknown to the given literal. The only way to write "treat unverifiable as satisfied", and always listed as a weakening in the consequence preview.

place.is.description: A user-named place. Makes the host's location sensing load-bearing; permanently unknown on a host without it.

time.localHourIn.description: Half-open local-hour window [from, to). Resolves unknown unless the clock is attested (P-R13).

approval.by.description: A role name bound to an approver identity. Rebinding the name is itself an amendment, not configuration (P-R12).

approval.byOrg.description: A role name bound to an organisational approver key.

user.typedPhrase.description: The user typing an exact phrase. false on an explicit refusal, unknown on timeout.

Term.description: An attribute of the artifact or installation. Artifact terms are always decidable from the package and never resolve to unknown.
